Describe the content for one placeholder

define_content.Rd

Says what should replace a placeholder and how it goes in. The code in content isn't run now: it's written into the Markdown by replace_placeholders() and runs when Quarto renders the document. Collect the results with placeholder_map().

Usage

define_content(
  description = NULL,
  placeholder_id,
  output_mode = c("inline", "chunk", "asis"),
  content,
  content_type = NULL,
  chunk_options = list()
)

Arguments

description

Optional. A short description of the content, shown in the validation log to help you check the right output is in the right place.

placeholder_id

The part of the placeholder after the prefix. With the default prefix "placeholder_", the ID "plot" fills placeholder_plot.

output_mode

How the content goes in:

  • "inline" writes inline R code, `r <content>`, for a value inside a sentence.

  • "chunk" writes a code chunk on its own line, for plots, tables or anything longer. The chunk is R unless you set chunk_options$engine.

  • "asis" writes text exactly as given. If content is a string it's inserted as it is; otherwise the code itself is inserted as text, not its result.

content

The code to insert, for example { plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg) } or nrow(mtcars). It can also be passed in from a function or with !!, for example inside lapply().

content_type

Optional. A label such as "plot", "table" or "qmd", shown in the validation log.

chunk_options

A named list of chunk options, used when output_mode = "chunk". Any knitr option works, such as echo = FALSE or fig.width = 7. Three more control how the chunk is written:

  • engine: the chunk language. Defaults to "r".

  • as_child: if TRUE, write the chunk to its own file, child_<id>.qmd, and include that file instead.

  • child_dir: the folder for child files, relative to the Markdown file.

Value

A content_spec object, to pass to placeholder_map().

See also

Other content: placeholder_map()

Examples

plot <- define_content(
  placeholder_id = "plot",
  description = "Car weight against fuel economy",
  output_mode = "chunk",
  content = { plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg) },
  chunk_options = list(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7)
)

total <- define_content(
  placeholder_id = "total",
  output_mode = "inline",
  content = nrow(mtcars)
)
